hook: SCP-4062 is a good dog with one unusual habit, and a Soviet submarine attached to its story. The file starts like a pet-care sheet and ends in an interview that gets funnier the more seriously everyone takes it.
whyItMatters:
The entry is a straight-faced comedy that grows a whole alternate world out of one physical gag. A dog that shakes itself dry is ordinary; a dog that shakes hard enough to boil water becomes an engine, and the article follows that logic all the way into submarine design and superpower politics.

It also has a soft center: a footnote records that the Ethics Committee replaced the cheap pressure-vessel containment with walks, toys and feeding for the dog's emotional wellbeing.
thingsToNotice:
The dog was found powering a Soviet attack submarine, K-406, in place of the expected reactor, and only its engineer knew. He insists he is a canine engineer from a canine physics program, that his boat was a sheepdog-class vessel called K-968, and that the superpowers are locked in a standoff over canine bombs and missiles.

Notice how the interviewer keeps correcting him and he keeps not understanding the word nuclear. The footnotes add to the joke, especially his claim that the dog has a half-life and will eventually decay into a husky and two toy terriers, and the log closes with him sighing and offering to draw a diagram.
